title: Flowise organization billing -- T1548 attacker-supplied subscriptionId reaches another tenant's Stripe subscription
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70476 (GHSA-gmmw-qg98-6j6p),
affecting Flowise's organization billing endpoints.

`updateSubscriptionPlan` and `updateAdditionalSeats` in
`organization.controller.ts` take `subscriptionId` directly from the
request body and forward it to the Stripe integration layer, with no
check that the identifier belongs to the authenticated user's own
organization. The server trusts the client-supplied Stripe
subscription ID rather than resolving it from the caller's session
context. Any authenticated user of ANY organization can supply
another organization's `subscriptionId` (obtainable via the
organization read endpoint or other exposed references) and
downgrade its plan, change its seat quantity, or otherwise trigger
billing operations against a tenant they have no relationship to.

Detection logic flags a `POST /api/v1/organization/update-subscription-plan`
or `POST /api/v1/organization/update-additional-seats` request whose
`subscriptionId` in the body does not match the caller's own
organization's subscription -- the exact ownership-unchecked pattern
this advisory's proof of concept demonstrates end-to-end (leak a
victim `subscriptionId`, then downgrade or zero its seats from an
unrelated account).

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the exact controller functions, source files, and a full
request/response proof of concept), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
